chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated, from his father, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from some of our scholars, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the body and image, so he replied in writing: 'Glory be to Him who has nothing whatsoever like unto Him, and who is devoid of both body and image.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim say about Allah's body and image?
ai.summary: This correspondence from Imam al-Kadhim (AS) to his companion clarifies the doctrine of divine incorporeality (Tajsim) by affirming that Allah is free from physical dimensions, serving as a foundational text for Shia theological debates against the Mu'tazila and Asha'ira. The response echoes the Quranic declaration of absolute transcendence, reinforcing the principle that God's essence is distinct from created matter and spatial limitations.
